package_info.package_versions: Unknown (all versions distributed via Google Play Store and 9Apps during campaign)
package_info.why_malicious: The package is malicious because it masquerades as a legitimate app, exploits Android vulnerabilities to silently modify pre-installed applications, and injects code that displays fraudulent ads. This subverts Android's app sandboxing, abuses device permissions, and enables large-scale ad fraud without user consent, undermining device integrity and user trust.

execution_context.trigger: post-installation, during runtime of the malicious app
execution_context.file_location: Injected into pre-installed application APK files after initial installation of the malicious app

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After installation, the code scans for vulnerable pre-installed apps, injects malicious ad-displaying code into their APKs, and reinstalls the modified apps, resulting in unauthorized ad injection and persistent ad fraud at runtime.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code modifies other installed applications by injecting malicious code, which is highly abnormal and a strong indicator of malware. Legitimate Android apps do not patch or replace other apps' APKs, especially without user consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Android apps are sandboxed and do not alter or repackage other installed applications. This behavior violates Android's security model, user trust, and app store policies.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System update tools or device management software (with explicit user consent and system-level privileges) may update or patch apps, but do not inject adware or unauthorized code.
key_indicators: Scans for and modifies other installed apps' APK files
Injects ad-displaying code into unrelated applications
Reinstalls patched APKs without user knowledge or consent

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when a compromised, patched app is launched)
execution_context.file_location: Injected ad module within the code of patched APKs
required_permissions: network (to fetch ad content from remote servers)
display_overlay (to show ads over legitimate app UI)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a compromised app is launched, the injected code fetches ad content from a remote attacker-controlled server and displays fraudulent ads as overlays within the app, generating illicit revenue for the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Displaying ads via injected code in unrelated apps is a hallmark of adware and fraudulent monetization. The code operates without user consent, outside the original app's intent, and communicates with attacker-controlled infrastructure.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps display ads only within their own context and with user awareness. Injecting ads into other apps' UI is deceptive, violates user expectations, and breaches app store policies.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Ad SDKs in legitimate apps display ads, but only within the app's own UI and with user consent. They do not inject ad modules into unrelated apps.
key_indicators: Fetches ad content from non-standard, attacker-controlled servers
Displays overlay ads in unrelated or system apps
Operates without user interaction or consent
Ad module code present in apps that should not contain advertising functionality

attack_chain.action: User installs a seemingly innocent app from Google Play Store or 9Apps.
attack_chain.leads_to: Initial infection and execution of malicious payload

attack_chain.action: Malware scans the device for vulnerable pre-installed apps and injects malicious ad code into their APKs.
attack_chain.leads_to: Patched apps with embedded adware are installed

attack_chain.action: Patched apps, when launched, execute injected code to fetch and display fraudulent ads.
attack_chain.leads_to: Continuous ad fraud and revenue generation for attacker

behavioral_signatures: App attempts to modify or replace other installed APKs on the device
Injected code in unrelated apps displays ads or overlays unexpectedly
Unexpected network requests from system or pre-installed apps to non-standard ad servers
file_indicators: APK files with unexpected code sections or embedded ad modules
Repackaged APKs with altered digital signatures or mismatched certificates
Presence of adware modules in apps that are not supposed to display ads
network_indicators: Outbound connections from system or pre-installed apps to known ad fraud or attacker-controlled domains
Frequent ad content fetches from non-standard ad networks or suspicious remote servers
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for apps that attempt to modify or reinstall other APKs, especially those that inject ad modules into unrelated apps. Analyze network traffic for unexpected ad content requests originating from system or pre-installed apps. Use file integrity checks to detect repackaged APKs and scan for known adware code signatures within app packages. Correlate behavioral, file, and network indicators to identify devices compromised by Agent Smith.
